p.src: Meanwhile, Xichun was studying a manual of go when she suddenly heard someone in the courtyard calling for Caiping. It was none other than Yuanyang. Caiping went out and returned with Yuanyang. Yuanyang had brought a young maid carrying a small parcel of yellow silk. Xichun asked with a smile, “What is it?” Yuanyang replied, “Her Ladyship will be eighty-one next year, an ominous ninth year. She has vowed to sponsor nine days and nights of religious observances and has resolved to have 3,651 copies of the Diamond Sutra transcribed. Those have already been sent out for people outside the household to copy. But there is a common saying that the Diamond Sutra is like the outer casing of a Daoist talisman, while the Heart Sutra is its potent core. Therefore, copies of the Heart Sutra must be interspersed among the Diamond Sutras to gain still greater merit. Her Ladyship considers the Heart Sutra even more important, and since Guanzizai is a female bodhisattva, she wants the ladies and young mistresses of the family to copy 365 of them, which will be both more devout and more pure. In our household, Second Mistress is excepted: first, she manages the household and has no time; second, she cannot write it. All the other women who can write have been allotted some, however many or few—even Mistress Zhen and the concubines in the Eastern Mansion, to say nothing of the ladies in this house.” Xichun nodded when she heard this. “There is little else I can do, but when it comes to copying sutras, I am most devout. Set it down and have some tea.” Only then did Yuanyang set the little parcel on the table and sit down with Xichun. Caiping poured her a cup of tea. Xichun asked with a smile, “Will you be copying any?” “You are teasing me again, miss,” said Yuanyang. I managed well enough some years ago, but in the last three or four years, have you ever seen me so much as pick up a brush?” “But this is an act of merit,” said Xichun. Yuanyang said, “I have something of my own as well. For more than three years now, after settling Her Ladyship for the night, I have been reciting the Buddha’s name over grains of rice. I have kept that rice safely, and when Her Ladyship performs these rites, I shall add it to the offerings for the Buddha and the food distributed in charity. That will be my own small token of devotion.” Xichun said, “In that case, if Her Ladyship becomes Guanyin, you will be the Dragon Girl at her side.” Yuanyang replied, “I could never aspire to such a blessed station. Yet apart from Her Ladyship, I seem incapable of serving anyone else. Who knows what bond was formed between us in a former life?” As she spoke, she rose to leave and told the young maid to open the little silk parcel. Taking something out, she said, “This bundle of plain paper is for copying the Heart Sutra.” Then she picked up a packet of Tibetan incense and said, “This is to be burned while you copy the sutra.” Xichun agreed to everything.

p.src: Yuanyang then took her leave and returned with the young maid to Grandmother Jia’s apartments, where she reported what had happened. She found Grandmother Jia playing backgammon with Li Wan and stood beside them to watch. Li Wan threw good dice and knocked several of the old lady’s pieces off the board. Yuanyang pressed her lips together to hide a smile. Suddenly Baoyu came in carrying two little cages woven from fine bamboo strips, with several katydids inside. “I heard that Grandmother has trouble sleeping at night,” he said, “so I brought these for her amusement.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “Just because your father is away, do not think you can get up to all the mischief you please.” Baoyu laughed. “I have not been getting into mischief.” “If you have not,” said Grandmother Jia, “why are you playing with such things instead of studying in the schoolroom?” “I did not get them for myself,” said Baoyu. Today the tutor asked Huan and Lan to compose matching couplet lines. Huan could not think of one, so I quietly prompted him. When he gave the answer, the tutor was pleased and praised him twice. He was grateful to me, so he bought these as a respectful present. So I brought them as a respectful present for Grandmother.” Grandmother Jia said, “Does he not study every day? Why could he not compose the matching line? If he cannot do it, have your Great-uncle Ru slap his face and see whether that shames him. And you have some nerve! Have you forgotten how, when your father was home, the mere order to write a poem or lyric frightened you into looking like a little ghost? Yet now you are boasting again. That boy Huan is even more hopeless. After begging someone to do his work for him, he finds some devious way to reward the favor. Such a little child already up to sly tricks and not even ashamed! Who knows what sort of creature he will become when he grows up?” At this, everyone in the room burst out laughing. Grandmother Jia then asked, “And what of young Lan? Did he manage to answer? This time Huan ought to have helped him, since Lan is younger than he is. Is that not so?” Baoyu laughed. “He did not need any help; he composed it himself.” Grandmother Jia said, “I do not believe it. Otherwise, you must have played some trick for him too. You are quite extraordinary nowadays—‘a camel has run out from among the sheep, and you alone tower over them all.’ So now you can write essays as well!” Baoyu laughed. “He truly did compose it himself. The tutor even praised him and said that he was certain to make something of himself one day. If Grandmother does not believe me, send someone to fetch him and test him yourself. Then you will know.” Grandmother Jia said, “If that is truly so, I shall be pleased. I was only afraid that you were lying. Since he did compose it himself, the child may indeed show some promise when he grows up.”

p.src: Then, looking at Li Wan, she thought of Jia Zhu again. “Your elder brother did not die in vain after all. Your sister-in-law has devoted herself to raising this boy, and one day he will uphold your elder brother’s household and carry on his line.” At these words, she could not keep the tears from flowing. Li Wan was deeply moved by this, but seeing that the Lady Dowager was already grieving, she hastily held back her own tears and consoled her with a smile: “This is all thanks to the blessings Your Ladyship’s accumulated virtue has left us. We merely live under the shelter of your good fortune. If only he can live up to what Your Ladyship has said, that will be our great good fortune. You are pleased with him when you look at him, so why should you make yourself sad?” Then she turned to Baoyu and said, “Uncle Bao, you must not praise him so much in future. He is only a little boy—what can he possibly understand? You mean only to show your affection for him, but he cannot understand that. If this goes on, he will grow vain and ambitious, and how will he ever make further progress?” “Your sister-in-law is right about that too,” said the Lady Dowager. Only, he is still very young, so you must not press him too hard. Children are timid. If you drive him too hard and make him ill, not only will he be unable to study, but all your efforts will have been wasted.” When the Lady Dowager said this, Li Wan could restrain herself no longer. Tears streamed down her cheeks, and she hurriedly wiped them away.

p.src: Just then Jia Huan and Jia Lan also came in and paid their respects to the Lady Dowager. Jia Lan first greeted his mother, then went over and stood in attendance beside the Lady Dowager. The Lady Dowager said, “I just heard your uncle say that you composed an excellent matching line and that your teacher praised you.” Jia Lan said nothing, but merely smiled with his lips pursed. Yuanyang came over and said, “May I inform Your Ladyship that supper is ready?” “Go and invite your aunt,” said the Lady Dowager. Hupo at once sent someone to Lady Wang’s quarters to invite Aunt Xue. Meanwhile, Baoyu and Jia Huan withdrew. Suyun and the young maids came over and put away the backgammon set. Li Wan remained to wait upon the Lady Dowager at supper, and Jia Lan stood beside his mother. The Lady Dowager said, “You mother and son shall eat with me.” Li Wan assented. Presently the meal was served, and the maid returned to report: “Lady Wang asks me to tell Your Ladyship that Aunt Xue has been coming and going these past few days and could not come over personally to take her leave; she returned home after dinner today.” The Lady Dowager then had Jia Lan sit beside her, and they all ate together; there is no need to relate the details.

p.src: Now, when the Lady Dowager had finished supper and washed, she reclined on her bed and chatted idly. A young maid spoke to Hupo, who came over and reported to the Lady Dowager, “The master of the eastern mansion has come to wish Your Ladyship good night.” “Tell him that managing the household has left him tired these days, and that he should go and rest,” said the Lady Dowager. I know he has come.” The young maid told the older women servants, and only then did they convey the message to Jia Zhen. Jia Zhen then withdrew. The next day, Jia Zhen came over to attend to the various household affairs. The gate servants came one after another to report several matters. Then another young servant announced, “The estate steward has sent some fruit.” “Where is the list?” asked Jia Zhen. The young servant hurriedly presented it. When Jia Zhen looked at it, he saw that it listed nothing more than fresh seasonal fruits, together with various vegetables and game. After reading it, Jia Zhen asked who usually had charge of such deliveries. The gatekeeper replied, “Zhou Rui.” He therefore summoned Zhou Rui and said, “Check everything against the account, then take it inside and hand it over properly. Wait while I make a copy of the incoming account, so that we shall have a record for comparison.” He also ordered, “Tell the kitchen to add several dishes to the meal for the men who brought the fruit, and give them their customary food and gratuity.” Zhou Rui assented. He had the goods moved to Xifeng’s courtyard while carefully handing over both the estate accounts and the fruit. After going out for a while, he returned and asked Jia Zhen, “Did you count the fruit that just arrived, sir?” “How could I possibly have time to count such things?” said Jia Zhen. I gave you the account; just count them against it.” Zhou Rui said, “I have counted them. Nothing is missing, but there are no extras either. Since you have kept a copy, sir, you should call the men who delivered the fruit back and ask whether their account is genuine or false.” “What do you mean by that?” said Jia Zhen. “They are only a few pieces of fruit; what does it matter? I was not suspecting you.” As he spoke, Bao Er came in, kowtowed, and said, “Please, sir, let me serve outside as I did before.” Jia Zhen said, “What is the matter with you two now?” Bao Er said, “A servant like me has no right to say anything here.” “Who asked you to say anything?” said Jia Zhen. Bao Er said, “Why should I stay here merely to keep watch on others?” Zhou Rui broke in: “I manage the rents and estates here, and every year three to five hundred thousand taels pass through my hands, yet the masters, mistresses, and young ladies have never said a word about it—much less about such trifling articles as these. If Bao Er’s words are to be believed, all the masters’ fields and houses must already have been made away with by us servants.” Jia Zhen thought, “Bao Er must have been quarrelling here. I had better send him outside.”

p.src: Jia Zhen was resting in a side room when he heard a tremendous commotion at the gate. He sent someone to investigate, who returned and reported, “Bao Er and Zhou Rui’s godson are fighting.” “Who is Zhou Rui’s godson?” asked Jia Zhen. The gatekeeper replied, “His name is He San. He is a thoroughly tiresome fellow who drinks and makes trouble at home every day, and often comes to sit about at the gate. When he heard Bao Er and Zhou Rui quarrelling, he thrust himself into the dispute.” “That is intolerable,” said Jia Zhen. Tie up Bao Er and that fellow—He-something-or-other—together and bring them to me! Where is Zhou Rui?” The gatekeeper replied, “He left as soon as the fighting began.” “Bring him here!” ordered Jia Zhen. This is outrageous!” The servants acknowledged the order. While the uproar continued, Jia Lian returned, and Jia Zhen told him the whole story. “This is outrageous!” exclaimed Jia Lian. He sent still more men to seize Zhou Rui. Knowing there was no escaping them, Zhou Rui presented himself as well. Jia Zhen ordered all of them bound. Jia Lian said to Zhou Rui, “What passed between you earlier was no great matter. The elder master explained things, and that should have ended it. Why did you start fighting outside again? Fighting among yourselves was bad enough, yet you even brought in some mongrel outsider called He San to make trouble. Instead of bringing them under control, you simply walked away.” With that, he kicked Zhou Rui several times. “Beating Zhou Rui alone will do no good,” said Jia Zhen. He shouted an order that Bao Er and He San should each receive fifty lashes and be driven out. Only then did he confer with Jia Lian about their proper business. Behind their backs, the servants now began to spread all manner of gossip. Some said Jia Zhen was protecting his own; others said he had no idea how to settle a dispute; still others said he had never been a decent man in the first place. Had there not been all those scandals involving the You sisters? And was it not through his mediation that the Second Master had summoned Bao Er? If he now considered Bao Er useless, surely it was because Bao Er’s wife had failed to serve him to his satisfaction. With so many tongues wagging, opinions flew in every direction.

p.src: Now, ever since Jia Zheng had taken charge of the official seal at the Ministry of Works, many members of his household had found opportunities to enrich themselves. When Jia Yun heard of it, he too wanted a share of the business. He spoke to several foremen outside the household and agreed on his commission, then bought some fashionable embroidery with which to seek favour through Xifeng. Xifeng was in her room when she heard the maids say, “Both the elder and second masters are furious and are beating people outside.” Not knowing the cause, Xifeng was just about to send someone to inquire when Jia Lian came in and related everything that had happened outside. “The incident itself may not be serious,” said Xifeng, “but this sort of behaviour must never be allowed to become customary. Our house is still at the height of its prosperity, yet they already dare to fight. When the younger generation takes charge in future, they will be more uncontrollable still. The year before last, when I was at the eastern mansion, I saw Jiao Da with my own eyes, hopelessly drunk and lying beneath the steps, cursing everyone indiscriminately, high and low alike. He may have rendered distinguished service in the past, but the distinction between master and servant must still be observed, and some sense of propriety maintained. I do not mean to criticize Mistress Zhen, but she is too mild and honest; she has indulged every one of them until they acknowledge no restraint at all. And now there is this Bao Er. I had even heard that he was a useful man to both you and Cousin Zhen, so why did you beat him today?” Her words struck Jia Lian in a tender spot. Looking embarrassed, he evaded the subject and, on the pretext of having business to attend to, took his leave as he spoke.

p.src: Jia Yun smiled and followed him into the room. On seeing Xifeng, he paid his respects and said, “Mother sends her greetings.” Xifeng in turn asked after his mother. “What brings you here?” Xifeng asked. Jia Yun replied, “You were so good to me in the past, Aunt, that I think of it constantly and feel I can never repay you. I have wanted to show you my gratitude, but feared you might read too much into it. Now that the Double Ninth Festival is here, I have prepared a few trifles. There is nothing you lack, of course; they are merely a small token of your nephew’s devotion. I only fear you may refuse to do me the honor of accepting them.” Xifeng smiled. “Sit down and tell me what you have to say.” Only then did Jia Yun sit down sideways, hastily setting the gifts on a nearby table. Xifeng continued, “You are hardly a man of means. Why go spending money needlessly? It is not as though I were in need of these things. Tell me honestly what you had in mind in coming here today.” “I had nothing else in mind,” said Jia Yun. “I merely felt so indebted for your kindness that I had to do something.” As he spoke, he smiled faintly. “That will not do,” said Xifeng. I know very well how short of money you are. Why should I take things from you for nothing? If you want me to accept these gifts, you must first explain everything plainly. If you go on hinting at things without speaking out, I shall not accept them.” Left with no alternative, Jia Yun rose and said with an ingratiating smile, “I harbor no extravagant hopes. A few days ago I heard that Master is overseeing the imperial-tomb works. I have several friends who have handled many building projects and are thoroughly reliable, so I hoped you might put in a word for me with Master. If they could secure one or two contracts, I would never forget your kindness. And if there is anything the household needs done, I too can be of service to you.” Xifeng said, “If it were some other matter, I could make the decision. But in official affairs, the senior officials and department officers make the decisions above, while the clerks and runners carry them out below. I am afraid outsiders have no way to intervene. Even our own servants do no more than attend upon Master. Even when your Second Uncle goes there, it is only on each household’s private business; he cannot meddle in official matters either. As for household affairs, everyone here undermines someone else to gain an advantage, and even Cousin Zhen cannot keep them under control. You are young and junior in rank; how could you possibly manage such people? Besides, the work at the offices is nearly finished. There would be nothing for you to do but eat their food and run about to no purpose. There are any number of things you could do at home. Surely you will not starve without this particular livelihood. I am telling you the honest truth. Go home and think it over, and you will understand.

p.src: I appreciate your good intentions. Take the gifts back at once and return them to whoever supplied them.” As she was speaking, a large group of nursemaids came in with Qiaojie. Qiaojie was dressed in a dazzling profusion of brocade and flowers and carried a number of toys. Beaming with delight, she went up to Xifeng and began chattering about what she had heard. At the sight of her, Jia Yun rose and greeted her eagerly with a smile. “So this is my little cousin, is it? Would you like me to bring you something nice?” At that, Qiaojie suddenly burst into tears. Jia Yun hastily stepped back. “There, there, do not be afraid,” said Xifeng. She quickly gathered Qiaojie into her arms and said, “This is your big brother Yun. Why are you suddenly shy of him?” Jia Yun said, “My little cousin is a lovely child. She is destined for great good fortune.” Qiaojie turned to look at Jia Yun and began crying again; this happened several times in succession. Seeing how things stood, Jia Yun could no longer remain seated, so he rose, took his leave, and prepared to go. “Take your gifts with you,” said Xifeng. “Will you not even do me the honor of accepting this little token, Aunt?” asked Jia Yun. Xifeng replied, “If you do not take them, I shall have someone deliver them to your home. Brother Yun, do not behave like this. You are no outsider. If an opportunity arises here, I shall naturally send someone for you. If there is no work, nothing can be done; it is not a matter of these gifts.” Seeing that Xifeng was determined not to accept them, Jia Yun could only say with a flushed face, “In that case, I shall find something useful to bring you another time.” Xifeng then told Xiaohong to take the gifts and follow Jia Yun out to see him off.

p.src: As Jia Yun walked along, he thought to himself, “They say Second Mistress is formidable, and formidable she certainly is. She leaves not the slightest opening and is utterly decisive. No wonder she has no heir. That Qiaojie is stranger still: the sight of me affects her as if I were some enemy from a former life. What rotten luck! I have wasted the whole day for nothing.” Xiaohong was also displeased that Jia Yun had gained nothing and followed him out carrying the gifts. Jia Yun took the bundle, opened it, selected two items, and quietly offered them to Xiaohong. Xiaohong refused them, saying, “Please do not do this, Second Master. If Mistress finds out, it will look bad for us both.” “Take them and keep them safely,” said Jia Yun. “What is there to fear? How could she possibly find out? If you refuse them, it means you look down on me.” Only then did Xiaohong accept them with a faint smile, saying, “Who wants your things? They are hardly worth anything.” As soon as she had spoken, her face flushed crimson again. Jia Yun smiled too. “It is not the things that matter to me either. Besides, they are nothing of consequence.” As they spoke, the two of them reached the inner gate. Jia Yun tucked the remaining gifts back into the front of his robe. Xiaohong urged him, “You should go now. If anything comes up, feel free to seek me out. I am working in this courtyard now, so it will be easy to reach me.” Jia Yun nodded. “Second Mistress is so formidable that unfortunately I cannot come here often. In any case, you understand what I meant just now. I shall tell you more when there is time.” Her whole face glowing red, Xiaohong said, “Go now, but come and visit us often from tomorrow on. Who told you to remain so distant from her?” “I understand,” said Jia Yun. With that, Jia Yun went out through the courtyard gate. Xiaohong remained standing in the gateway, gazing after him in a daze until he had disappeared into the distance; only then did she go back inside.

p.src: Meanwhile, in her room, Xifeng ordered dinner to be prepared and then asked, “Have you cooked the congee?” The maids hurried away to inquire and returned to report, “It is ready.” Xifeng said, “Then serve a dish or two of those wine-pickled things from the south.” Qiutong acknowledged the order and told the maids to attend to it. Ping’er came over and said with a smile, “I nearly forgot. At noon today, while you were with the Old Lady in the upper quarters, the abbess of Water-Moon Convent sent someone to ask you for two jars of southern pickles and several months of her allowance in advance, saying that she was unwell. I asked the Taoist nun who came, ‘What is wrong with your mistress?’ She said, ‘It has been four or five days. The night before last, several of the girls among the young Buddhist and Taoist novices went to sleep without putting out their lamps, though she had warned them repeatedly. That night, seeing their lamps still burning after midnight, she called for them to put them out; but every one of them was asleep, and no one answered, so she had to get up and extinguish the lamps herself. When she returned to her kang, she saw two people, a man and a woman, sitting upon it. She hastily demanded to know who they were, whereupon they slipped a rope around her neck, and she cried out for help. Hearing her, everyone lit lamps and rushed in together. She was already lying on the floor, frothing at the mouth, but fortunately they managed to revive her. Even now she cannot eat, and that is why she sent me to seek some pickles.’ Since you were not in your room, I did not think it proper to give them to her. I said, ‘Her Ladyship has no time just now, for she is in the upper quarters. I shall tell her when she returns.’ Then I sent her away. I only remembered when I heard southern preserves mentioned just now; otherwise it would have slipped my mind entirely.” Xifeng listened, momentarily dazed, then said, “There are still some southern pickles left, are there not? Just have someone send some over. As for the money, have Brother Qin come and collect it in a day or two.” Just then Xiaohong entered and reported, “Second Master has sent word that he has business outside the city tonight and cannot return, so he wished to notify you beforehand.” “Very well,” said Xifeng.

p.src: As she spoke, a young maid came running from the rear, shouting and gasping for breath, straight into the courtyard. Outside, Ping’er met her, and several other maids joined them in whispering together. Xifeng asked, “What are you talking about?” Ping’er replied, “The little maid is rather timid and is telling ghost stories.” Xifeng summoned the young maid inside and asked, “What ghost story?” The maid said, “I just went to the back to tell the odd-job servants to add coal. I heard a clattering noise in the three empty rooms and thought it was cats or rats, but then I heard a sigh, just like a person breathing out. I was frightened, so I ran back.” Xifeng scolded her: “Nonsense! I will not tolerate talk of spirits and ghosts here. I have never believed such things. Now get out, quickly!” The young maid withdrew. Xifeng then had Caiming check through the accounts for the day’s miscellaneous household expenses. By then it was nearly the second watch. They all rested a while longer and exchanged a little idle talk, after which she told everyone to retire. Xifeng also went to bed. Near the third watch, while Xifeng hovered between sleep and wakefulness, the hairs on her body suddenly stood on end, startling her awake. The longer she lay there, the more a chill crept over her, so she called Ping’er and Qiutong to keep her company. Neither woman understood what was troubling her. Qiutong had never been well disposed toward Xifeng. Later, after the affair of Second Sister You, Jia Lian had ceased to cherish her so much, while Xifeng had taken pains to win her over. She was now quiet enough, but inwardly she was far less devoted than Ping’er and merely maintained an appearance of affection. Seeing that Xifeng was unwell, she had no choice but to bring her some tea. Xifeng took a sip and said, “Thank you for your trouble. Go to sleep; Ping’er alone will be enough here.” But Qiutong wished to display her attentiveness and said, “Since you cannot sleep, madam, the two of us might as well take turns sitting with you.” Even as Xifeng spoke, she fell asleep. When Ping’er and Qiutong saw that Xifeng was asleep, they heard roosters crowing in the distance. Only then did they lie down for a short while without undressing. Soon it was daylight, and they hurriedly rose to help Xifeng wash and dress. Because of what had happened during the night, Xifeng remained distracted and uneasy; yet stubbornly refusing to show weakness, she still forced herself to rise. As she sat there brooding, she suddenly heard a young maid call from the courtyard, “Is Miss Ping in the room?” Ping’er answered, and the young maid lifted the curtain and entered. Madam Wang had sent her to find Jia Lian. She said, “Someone outside has come to report an urgent official matter. The Master has only just gone out, so Madam asks that Second Master come over at once.” Xifeng started in alarm when she heard this. What the matter was will be revealed in the next chapter.
